tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session logs show a full demonstration: login (handled outside tool), enumerate filter controls, close notification popup, populate filter inputs (ID from/to, first/last name, email, IP address, session start/last activity ranges, type select, last URL), click Search, extract grid rows (none in sample), click a column header to sort by ID, then Reset filters and verify cleared. The session provides stable elementHash values for several interacted controls and robust XPath fallbacks for others.

Task Definition:
- Create a deterministic, re-usable tool that navigates to the Magento Online Customers admin page, fills the filter controls with parameterized values, applies the Search, extracts the grid rows & pagination state, sorts by ID (demonstration), then resets filters and returns the post-reset input values.

Action Plan (step-by-step):
1. Navigate to the provided Online Customers admin URL ({base_url}).
2. Wait for the page to load briefly.
3. Close the "Incoming Message" notification popup (stable elementHash recorded) so filters are accessible.
4. Fill each filter input in a deterministic order using recorded elementHash where available, otherwise use the grid-anchored XPath selectors. Values are taken directly from inputs to avoid conditional branching (empty values are allowed).
   - ID From, ID To, First Name, Last Name, Email, IP Address, Session Start From/To, Last Activity From/To, Type select, Last URL.
5. Click the Search button (recorded elementHash) to apply filters.
6. Wait and extract the grid rows and pagination state (returns rows array and selectors for row cell extraction).
7. Click the ID header (elementHash recorded) to demonstrate sorting by ID, wait and re-extract the first 5 row IDs.
8. Click Reset Filter (elementHash recorded) and wait; then extract current filter input values to confirm reset.

Variable Identification (inputs required by tool):
- base_url (required): URL to navigate to the admin Online Customers page.
- customer_id_from, customer_id_to: numeric/string ID range fields (optional)
- first_name, last_name, email, ip_address: text filters (optional)
- session_start_from, session_start_to, last_activity_from, last_activity_to: date/time strings (optional)
- type: select option for 'Type' filter (enum: 'customer','visitor','either') (optional)
- last_url: text filter for Last URL (optional)
- per_page (optional): rows per page value (20/30/50/100/200) — not strictly required but included for completeness
- sort_by (optional): reserved but the recorded demo sorts by ID only; kept for future extension (enum of known sortable columns). For deterministic behavior we still click the recorded 'ID' header.

Step Optimization / Notes:
- Use recorded elementHash values for popup close, input fields and buttons when available (more stable than class-based selectors). Where elementHash is not available for a particular control (some date inputs), use the robust XPath anchored to the table that contains the 'ID' header.
- Avoid conditional branching: every input step writes the provided parameter (if empty it writes empty string), which keeps sequence deterministic.
- Navigation is used instead of indirect clicks where possible; no authentication steps are included because the demonstration started from an authenticated session.
- The tool avoids the previously failing 'storage_state' pattern (per developer note) by requiring a live authenticated context and not importing storage_state. If authentication is needed, callers should perform login externally before invoking this tool.

Selectors used (from recorded session):
- Popup close: elementHash = 'df76c6ce85'
- ID From input: elementHash = '39a8e4b87a'
- ID To input: elementHash = '6662425bd9'
- First Name input: elementHash = 'f70a21afd3'
- Last Name input: elementHash = 'a11d237c43'
- Email input: elementHash = '2e6ef5fa64'
- Type select: elementHash = '068ccb660c'
- Last URL input: elementHash = '5e5ed49cc3'
- Search button: elementHash = 'cdb786816b'
- ID header (sort): elementHash = '84558eb4dc'
- Reset Filter button: elementHash = 'a623d67807'
- Fallback XPaths anchored to the grid are used for IP and date inputs (td[6], td[7], td[8]).

Deterministic guarantees:
- Every click/input references either an elementHash captured in the demonstration (preferred) or a grid-anchored XPath that targets exactly one element in the standard Magento admin layout. This minimizes "locator resolved to multiple elements" failures.

Assumptions & Limitations:
- Caller provides a valid authenticated admin browser/session. The tool does not perform login.
- If the environment has a customized admin theme that changes the grid structure (hidden columns, reordered columns), the nth-child XPaths may need adjustment; however the elementHash-based selectors should still point to the recorded controls in the tested environment.
name: magento_admin_online_customers_filter_and_extract
description: Navigate to Magento admin Online Customers grid, populate the grid filters (ID range, names, email, IP, session times, last activity, Type, Last URL), apply Search, extract grid rows, optionally sort by ID, then Reset filters and confirm. Assumes the automation context is already authenticated into the Magento admin and page is reachable at the provided base_url.

steps.description: Open the Magento Online Customers admin page at the provided URL.
Wait briefly for the admin page and grid to render.
Close the 'Incoming Message' notification popup (recorded close link elementHash).
Enter ID 'From' into the ID range filter (first input in ID column).
Enter ID 'To' into the ID range filter (second input in ID column).
Enter First Name filter value.
Enter Last Name filter value.
Enter Email filter value.
Enter IP Address filter value (grid-anchored XPath fallback for IP column input).
Enter Session Start 'From' datetime (first input in Session Start column).
Enter Session Start 'To' datetime (second input in Session Start column).
Enter Last Activity 'From' datetime (first input in Last Activity column).
Enter Last Activity 'To' datetime (second input in Last Activity column).
Set the Type select: 'customer'/'visitor'/'either' (the select_text value is used directly; supply 'either' to leave default).
Enter Last URL filter value (partial path allowed).
Click the Search (Apply Filters) button to apply the filter values.
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
Capture all data rows after applying filters. If no rows are present, returns empty rows array and pagination info.
steps.goal: Extract visible data rows from the Online Customers grid and the pagination state (rows, total_records, per_page). Return a data structure with row cells for ID, First Name, Last Name, Email, IP, Session Start, Last Activity, Type, Last URL.

steps.description: Click the ID column header to toggle sort by ID (recorded elementHash for ID header).
Wait for the grid to re-sort.
Return the list of IDs from the first up-to-5 visible rows.
steps.goal: Extract the first 5 row IDs (or fewer) after sorting to demonstrate sorting took effect.

steps.description: Click the Reset Filter button to clear all filter fields.
Wait for the grid to refresh and filters to reset.
Return a map of filter input selectors and their current values after reset.
steps.goal: Read current values of the filter inputs to confirm reset (return each filter's 'value' where applicable).

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the Magento Online Customers admin page (example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/customer_online/')

input_schema.name: customer_id_from
input_schema.description: ID 'From' value for the ID range filter (use numeric string). Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: customer_id_to
input_schema.description: ID 'To' value for the ID range filter (use numeric string). Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: first_name
input_schema.description: First name filter text. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: last_name
input_schema.description: Last name filter text. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Email address filter text. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: ip_address
input_schema.description: IP address filter text (supports IPv4/IPv6). Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: session_start_from
input_schema.description: Session Start 'From' datetime. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (Magento datepicker format may vary). Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: session_start_to
input_schema.description: Session Start 'To' datetime. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: last_activity_from
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'From' datetime. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: last_activity_to
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'To' datetime. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Type filter. Use 'customer' to select Customer, 'visitor' to select Visitor, or 'either' to leave default/unselected.

input_schema.name: last_url
input_schema.description: Last URL filter (partial path allowed, e.g. '/checkout/cart'). Leave empty to not set.

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Rows per page value to use on the grid (20,30,50,100,200). Leave empty to keep current.
